name: Fügenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Rural scattered settlement above Fügen, featuring traditional farming and a breathtaking Alpenpanorama.
beschreibung:
Overview

Fügenberg is located in the front Zillertal in the Tyrolean district of Schwaz, spreading across the sunny slopes on the western side of the valley above Fügen. Covering an area of more than 58 square kilometres, Fügenberg is one of the largest municipalities in the valley, extending from gentle meadows at around 680 metres above sea level up into high alpine peaks exceeding 2,500 metres. Approximately 1,530 inhabitants live across the scenic districts of Fügenberg, Pankrazberg, and the high-altitude resort of Hochfügen in the picturesque Finsingtal. Fügenberg is characterised by the captivating contrast between peaceful mountain farming traditions and world-class alpine winter sports infrastructure. From the panoramic mountain hillsides, visitors enjoy wide open views across the entire valley toward the Rofan Mountains and the Zillertal Alps.

History

Settlement of the sunny slopes began in the High Middle Ages as clearing expanded when the flood-prone valley floor could no longer support the growing population. The settlement was first documented in 1315 as Fügerberg, while the prominent Pankrazberg was historically known as Swentperg. Between the 15th and 18th centuries, the area experienced economic prosperity driven by mining; miners extracted high-grade iron ore in the Finsingtal, at Arzjoch, and in the Öxltal to supply local smelting furnaces. Following the Napoleonic Wars and the return of Tyrol to Austria, the communities of Fügenberg and Pankrazberg were officially united into a single municipality in 1816. The cultural landmark of the area is the pilgrimage church of St. Pankraz, built between 1494 and 1497 in Late Gothic style by local miners and farmers. The church houses magnificent Baroque altars from 1697, a celebrated weather bell cast in 1582, and an artistic 18th-century Nativity crib.

Getting There

By car, visitors reach Fügenberg via the Inntal Autobahn A12, taking the exit Wiesing/Zillertal and following the Zillertalstraße B169 to Fügen. From the town centre, the well-maintained provincial road L218 winds uphill to Fügenberg and Pankrazberg. A toll-free scenic mountain road leads 12 kilometres further into the high valley to Hochfügen, where proper winter equipment is essential during snowfall. Rail travellers arrive at the major junction of Jenbach aboard ÖBB or DB trains and transfer to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn, running every half hour to Fügen-Hart station. From the station, regional VVT bus routes serve the mountain communities, while frequent free ski shuttles transport winter guests directly to the slopes of Hochfügen throughout the winter season.

Tips

During the winter months, Hochfügen at 1,500 to 2,500 metres altitude serves as a snow-sure paradise linked via the Wedelexpress with the Kaltenbach-Hochzillertal ski area, offering a combined 88 kilometres of groomed pistes. Freeriders revere the demanding powder bowls of the Finsingtal, while families enjoy the illuminated natural toboggan run. In summer, the Four Alms Hike starting from Hochfügen via the Lamarkalm, Pfundsalm, and Viertleralm invites hikers to sample local specialities like Zillertaler Krapfen and Graukäse. Alpine ascents up Gilfert at 2,506 metres or across toward Kellerjoch reward mountaineers with grand vistas of the surrounding peaks. A leisurely stroll to the pilgrimage church of St. Pankraz offers one of the most rewarding panoramic viewpoints over the lower Zillertal.
